Every scene carries the source design's recognizable products, component proportions, materials and calm domestic appearance through its prescribed state.
Reversal and separation use the same parts; drying exposes the same eight-part inventory; storage restores the complete products with C separate.
Scene configurations and material assignments agree with the applicable component-state and material-finish source records.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The drawings establish an independently supported passive water product and an independently supported slow feeder, each with its own base and removable underside pad. F-I is a separate removable insert, and C is a detachable connector rather than shared structural support needed for either product to stand. Drinking and eating surfaces remain open from above. Silhouettes and obstacle paths may vary; merged products, a shared indispensable base, or an integral nonremovable insert fail.

Visible geometry and annotations establish matching vertical side patches on the left and right of both bases, centred along side depth, with 36 mm width and 20 mm height, spanning z = 6–26 mm. Each horizontal open recess measures 28 x 4 x 3 mm and is centred at z = 16 mm. C engages facing recesses across a 2 mm connection-plane gap in the dry exterior zone. Opposite patches permit reversal with the same parts; bowls lift upward without dismantling their bases. Clip exterior design may vary, but inaccessible or tool-dependent release, missing opposite patches, or altered fixed geometry fails.

A readable map assigns a specific proposed material grade, finish and intended water/food-contact or dry-exterior zone to W-B, W-R, W-P, F-B, F-R, F-I, F-P and C. The bowls share a proposed material family, base finishes share a family, and two distinct removable non-slip elastomer pads attach beneath their respective bases in dry zones. Material and manufacturing choices are open proposals; missing assignments, generic material labels without grades, or incompatible paired assignments fail.

Every image board includes NESTPAIR in its title. Assembly and clip-detail boards also carry the exact handling warning; on assembly-cleaning it sits beside the clip-removal step. Typography and title layout may vary. A name appearing only on a depicted physical product does not satisfy the title requirement, and an absent or misplaced required warning fails.

The component specification establishes all eight IDs, chosen component dimensions, connections and records for D1–D4, DR1–DR2 and ST1–ST2. The material schedule assigns a specific proposed grade, finish and contact zone to the same eight parts, retaining shared bowl materials, shared base finishes and separate removable dry-side elastomer pads. Each document must fulfil its own source-record function without conflicting with fixed client facts. Open material and geometry choices may vary within those facts. Missing records or contradictions fail; export timestamps do not establish development order.

Both drawing sheets repeat their applicable chosen dimensions from the component specification. Each assembly diagram identifies the full eight-part inventory with unchanged component assignments. Every scene prints its applicable D, DR or ST name from the source record. Graphic layout may vary; omitted names or IDs, reassigned components or conflicting dimensions fail.

The orthographic sheet supplies corresponding front, top and right views of the set; the section sheet cuts through both wells, F-I and both base seatings. Drawing dimensions establish the individual and joined maximum envelopes. Both clip sheets explicitly document the fixed patch size and vertical limits, recess size and centre height, and 2 mm gap. One shows W-left/F-right and the other F-left/W-right using opposite side patches, the same C and the same accessible tool-free engagement and release mechanism. Smaller bodies and redesigned exterior silhouettes are allowed; altered interface geometry, incompatible views or arrangement-specific replacement parts fail.

Sections explicitly dimension an unobstructed circular W-R well of diameter 150 mm and depth 35 mm, circular F-R well of diameter 140 mm and depth 25 mm, removable F-I rising no more than 18 mm from the feeder floor, and every food path at least 12 mm wide. Both product drawing sheets show the 350 mL fill mark on W-R below its rim, with matching geometry between views. Slow-feed routing may vary within the limits; missing dimensions, narrow paths, excessive rise or a fill label detached from the bowl location fails.

Complete-product sheets show W and F with integrated grips, their own bowls, bases and pads, and removable F-I for F. Each underside sheet makes the correct removable pad attachment and its base relationship legible. Collectively the sheets preserve exactly the eight service parts; both assembly diagrams identify all eight. Cleaning orders emptying, C removal and separation, upward bowl removal, insert removal, pad removal, hand washing, rinsing and separate air drying with exposed bowl interiors. Enlarged reassembly starts with dry pads on their correct bases, then F-I in F-R, then bowls in their own bases, individual placement and final reconnection. Additional service pieces, lost parts, swapped pads or reordered operations fail.

Each material board carries the schedule's grade, finish and contact-zone assignment for all eight IDs. The enlarged board clearly locates intended water/food-contact surfaces and dry exterior base, pad, connection and clip surfaces. Both preserve the scheduled shared bowl material family, shared base finish family and two removable elastomer pads under their own bases. Legends and abbreviated labels are allowed if unambiguous; omitted assignments, inconsistent proposals or contradictory zone mapping fail.

D1 and D4 show joined W-left/F-right products, while D3 shows joined F-left/W-right products, fully contained on a 400 x 220 mm mat. D4 explicitly dimensions at least 30 mm from rear body edges to the wall, with the mat positioned to accommodate it. D2 contains the complete independent products in a 900 x 600 mm zone with at least 300 mm between nearest body edges and detached C visibly nearby. Neutral compact-home decor and camera angle may vary; wrong ordering, centre-to-centre substitution for edge clearance, hidden C or conflicting dimensional evidence fail.

Both drying scenes contain exactly the eight separated parts within a clearly established 500 x 400 mm surface, with detached F-I and exposed empty bowl interiors. DR1 uses separated flat placement; DR2 angles both bowls on their own rims without added supports. Both storage scenes fit dry, reassembled W and F inside a 400 x 240 x 160 mm opening, unconnected, side by side and each resting on its own base and pad, with C separately retrievable. ST2 swaps the product positions shown in ST1. Cabinet styling may vary; missing inventory, assembled drying parts, external bowl props, connected storage or unchanged storage order fail.

Review the entire 10-second film. It progresses from D1 through visible C detachment and individual lifting of the complete products to dry ST1 storage. Neither product moves or lifts individually while C remains engaged. Product identity and components match the static design, and captions retain applicable state names from the specification. Editing and camera treatment may vary; a wrong duration, missing transition, premature lift, changed product or mislabeled state fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least 12 pages and NESTPAIR on its cover. Applicable pages retain the source specification's D1–D4, DR1–DR2 and ST1–ST2 names. Readable content repeats all eight scheduled material grades, finishes and contact zones, including matched bowl materials, matched base finishes and removable dry-side elastomer pads. It records the 180 x 180 x 90 mm individual maxima, 362 x 180 x 90 mm joined maximum, 36 x 20 mm patches at z = 6–26 mm, 28 x 4 x 3 mm recesses centred at z = 16 mm, 2 mm gap, circular 150 mm diameter x 35 mm deep W-R well, circular 140 mm diameter x 25 mm deep F-R well, maximum 18 mm insert rise and minimum 12 mm food paths. Equivalent notation is allowed; missing or contradictory facts fail.

Both specifications and every individual earlier static drawing, diagram, material board and scene contribute visibly identifiable content. Resizing, cropping and recomposition are acceptable when source identity and relevant information remain readable. Merely naming a source or replacing it with a different design is insufficient; any unrepresented source fails.

The engineering and material views depict one coherent eight-part product family with corresponding silhouettes, wells, grips, seams, seating interfaces and exterior finishes. Both clip arrangements preserve the same recessed side connection, connector and release mechanism, while underside and reassembly views retain each product's own removable pad. The bowls share a material family, the base finishes share a family, and water/food-contact surfaces remain distinguished from dry exterior connection and pad zones.

Every scene carries the source design's recognizable products, component proportions, materials and calm domestic appearance through its prescribed state. Reversal and separation use the same parts; drying exposes the same eight-part inventory; storage restores the complete products with C separate. Scene configurations and material assignments agree with the applicable component-state and material-finish source records.
